aliases: depresión de la frecuencia cardíaca fetal
es.summary: Caída transitoria de la frecuencia cardíaca fetal (FCF) por debajo de su línea de base, relacionada o no con las contracciones. Algunas listas lo escriben «DEEP». Su tipo indica la causa.
key_points: DIP I (temprana o precoz): baja y sube a la vez que la contracción, en espejo; se debe a compresión de la cabeza y es normal.
DIP II (tardía): empieza durante la contracción y termina después de ella; indica insuficiencia útero-placentaria e hipoxia fetal.
DIP variable (umbilical): caída brusca de al menos 15 lpm, en forma de «V» o «W», por compresión del cordón.
Desaceleración prolongada: dura de 2 a 10 minutos; es preocupante.
Regla VEAL CHOP: Variable–Cordón, Early (temprana)–Cabeza, Aceleración–OK, Late (tardía)–Placenta.

usage: Ejemplo: «FCF 135 lpm, variabilidad moderada, DIP II repetidos».
Se describe junto con la DU para saber si la caída coincide con la contracción.
nursing_care: Ante DIP II o variables repetidos: decúbito lateral, suspender la oxitocina, bolo de líquidos IV y oxígeno según protocolo.
Avisar al médico de inmediato y documentar las medidas.
Si hay DIP variables tras la ruptura de membranas, descartar prolapso del cordón.
Los DIP I se consideran normales; seguir vigilando la FCF.

en.summary: A temporary drop of the fetal heart rate (FHR) below its baseline, related or not to contractions (DIP in Spanish; some lists write it "DEEP"). Its type points to the cause.
key_points: Early deceleration (DIP I): gradual FHR declines that return to baseline, mirroring the uterine contraction; caused by fetal head compression and considered normal.
Late deceleration (DIP II): starts during a contraction and continues after the contraction ends; it is associated with uteroplacental insufficiency and fetal hypoxia.
Variable deceleration: an abrupt drop of at least 15 bpm, with a "V" or "W" shape, caused by compression of the umbilical cord.
Prolonged deceleration: lasts 2 to 10 minutes from onset to return to baseline; it is concerning.
VEAL CHOP rule: Variable–Cord, Early–Head, Acceleration–OK, Late–Placenta.

usage: Example: "FHR 135 bpm, moderate variability, repetitive late decelerations (DIP II)".
Described together with the contraction pattern (DU) to see whether the drop matches the contraction.
nursing_care: For repetitive late or variable decelerations: side-lying position, stop oxytocin, IV fluid bolus and oxygen per protocol.
Notify the provider right away and document the actions taken.
With variable decelerations after rupture of membranes, rule out cord prolapse.
Early decelerations are considered normal; keep monitoring the FHR.

sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Basic Terms of Fetal Heart Rate and Contraction Patterns

key_points.0.quote: Gradual FHR declines that then return to baseline, mirroring the uterine contraction, are called early decelerations .

key_points.1.quote: Late decelerations are nonreassuring and almost always indicate fetal hypoxia .

key_points.3.quote: Isolated, sporadic decelerations of at least 15 bpm from the FHR baseline that last 2 to 10 minutes from onset to return to baseline are called prolonged decelerations .
